;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Auno attack]]
**[[Boko Haram]] militants kill at least 30 people, burning them to death while they were sleeping in their vehicles in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. Women and children are [[kidnap]]ped. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-51445070 (BBC News)]
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**[[Turkey]] says [[Syrian Army|Syrian]] shelling killed five of [[Turkish Land Forces|its troops]] at an observation post at [[Taftanaz Military Airbase]] in [[Idlib Governorate]]. The Turkish government says it "retaliated against the attack to destroy all enemy targets and avenging our fallen troops". [https://apnews.com/6bc42af087748821ec99ae128c9e761d (AP News)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-51447114 (BBC News)]
**[[Russian Air Force|Russian]] and [[Syrian Air Force]] warplanes carry out airstrikes on civilian settlements in [[Aleppo Governorate|Aleppo]] and [[Idlib Governorate|Idlib]] provinces, killing at least 17 to 25 civilians including six children. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/syrian-russian-airstrikes-kill-17-civilians-in-idlib/1729063 (AA)] [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/russian-air-strikes-kill-5-civilians-in-syria-monitor/ar-BBZPLjy (MSN)] [https://www.dw.com/en/russian-airstrike-kills-civilians-in-syrias-aleppo-province-attack/a-52322455 (DW)]
**A [[car bomb]] kills four people and injures 15 others in the Turkish-occupied city [[Afrin, Syria|Afrin]], in [[Aleppo Governorate]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200210-syrian-army-shelling-kills-five-turkish-soldiers-in-idlib (France 24)]

;Business and economy
*[[Climate change mitigation]], [[Individual and political action on climate change]]
**Dozens of [[climate activist]]s surround the offices of [[United States|American]] [[investment management]] company [[BlackRock]] in central [[Paris]] and vandalize the building, demanding they [[Fossil fuel divestment|disinvest from the fossil fuel industry]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-climate-change-protest-blackrock/climate-activists-invade-blackrock-office-in-paris-idUSKBN2041X2 (Reuters)]
*[[Brexit]]
**[[Government of the United Kingdom|UK government]] minister [[Michael Gove]] says an IT system for the prospective "smart" border will not be ready before 2025. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/brexit-border-checks-trade-michael-gove-eu-a9328211.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.ft.com/content/37379a1e-4c28-11ea-95a0-43d18ec715f5 (''Financial Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus]], head of the [[World Health Organization]], warns that overseas cases of the virus could be the "tip of the iceberg". [https://news.yahoo.com/warns-overseas-virus-spread-may-tip-iceberg-025122072.html (Yahoo! News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mainland China]]
***In a rare public appearance and wearing a mask, [[Xi Jinping]] visits a hospital in [[Beijing]], and urges "more decisive measures" to combat the virus. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51448571 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*A court in [[Israel]] sentences [[Sheikh]] [[Raed Salah]] to 28 months in prison for "inciting to [[Palestinian political violence|terror]]". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/israel-sentences-islamic-movement-leader-raed-salah-28-months-200210103250740.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Chinese cyberwarfare]]
**A [[federal grand jury]] in the United States charges four members of [[China]]’s [[People's Liberation Army]] with the [[Equifax#May–July 2017 data breach|2017 Equifax hack]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/02/10/politics/equifax-chinese-military-justice-department/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Mohiussunnath Chowdhury]] is convicted of planning terrorist attacks in [[London]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/uk-51449757 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] files lawsuits against [[King County, Washington|King County]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]] and the state of [[New Jersey]] over their use of [[Sanctuary city|sanctuary cities]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-justice-immigration/u-s-justice-department-files-new-lawsuits-in-renewed-push-to-pressure-sanctuary-cities-idUSKBN2042JW?il=0 (Reuters)]
;Politics and elections
*The president of [[Germany]]'s [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU]] party, [[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]], announces that she will resign as the party's president and not be a candidate for the [[Chancellor of Germany|federal chancellorship]] in the [[Next German federal election|next election]]. [https://www.spiegel.de/politik/deutschland/annegret-kramp-karrenbauer-kuendigt-ruecktritt-als-cdu-chefin-an-a-7fae3f80-1509-4ec8-8143-45b500f19d3d (''Der Spiegel'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/10/annegret-kramp-karrenbauer-to-quit-as-cdu-leader-amid-far-right-firewall-row (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte|administration]] of Philippine President [[Rodrigo Duterte]] moves to cancel the franchise of [[ABS-CBN Corporation|ABS-CBN]], the Philippines' largest broadcast media network, by lodging a complaint against it to the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines]]. Members of the Philippine press condemn the actions in moving for the cancellation of the franchise of ABS-CBN. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/02/10/world/asia/philippines-abs-cbn-franchise.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.rappler.com/move-ph/251416-journalists-advocates-call-on-filipinos-support-abs-cbn (''Rappler'')] [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/725510/journalists-decry-quo-warranto-petition-vs-abs-cbn/story/ (''GMA News Online'')]
